probes.name: P1-http-arm-surrenders-again
probes.subject: .claude/hooks/_sonnet_classifier.py
probes.note: Reverts the s290 fix on the HTTP-error arm: the first 500 returns a manufactured pause instead of re-asking. The test's FIRST assertion (decision == 'pause') stays GREEN, because a manufactured pause is also a pause - which is the whole reason `transport` has to exist. The URLError and ValueError arms are untouched, so P9's and P2's tests stay green: that green is what rules out 'something unrelated broke'.

probes.name: P9-socket-timeout-arm-surrenders-again
probes.subject: .claude/hooks/_sonnet_classifier.py
probes.note: Splitting HTTP errors out of `timeout` gave the URLError path its own `except` with its own `continue`, so its retry can now be lost INDEPENDENTLY of the HTTP one. Before the split one probe covered both paths; after it, a single probe covering both would be a coverage gap wearing a green tick.

probes.name: P2-empty-envelope-surrenders-again
probes.subject: .claude/hooks/_sonnet_classifier.py
probes.new:
last = _pause(f"API response malformed: {exc}", transport=TRANSPORT_MALFORMED)
            return last
probes.note: The third arm, and it needs its own probe: an empty `message.content` raises ValueError, not a URL error at all. 74 of 187 measured records land here. Under this mutation both the HTTP and socket arms still retry, so P1's and P9's tests stay GREEN - one mutation, one assertion.

probes.name: P7-http-error-relabelled-as-timeout
probes.subject: .claude/hooks/_sonnet_classifier.py
probes.note: Restores exactly the pre-s290 label. This is the regression that matters historically: the record still carries '500' in `reason`, so the sibling assertion ('500' in reason) stays GREEN under this mutation - which is precisely how the mislabel survived a whole session's review. The green sibling is the point here, not an accident.

probes.name: P8-the-two-values-collapse-into-one
probes.subject: .claude/hooks/_sonnet_classifier.py
probes.note: Distinct from P7: P7 sends the HTTP arm to the wrong constant, this makes the two CONSTANTS equal. Either way the aggregate re-merges, and only an assertion that COMPARES the two values can see it - checking each label alone still passes. Reaches the difference assertion first, so the set-equality assertion below it is never evaluated.

probes.name: P3-budget-constant-drifts
probes.subject: .claude/hooks/_sonnet_classifier.py
probes.note: The budget is Cray's typed call (s290), not a tuning knob: it sets how long a Stop hook can block his turn (3 x up to 75s worst case). This witnesses the CONSTANT's value only - the behavioural claim that the loop actually runs three times is P6's, because a constant can read 3 while the loop ignores it.

probes.name: P6-loop-runs-one-attempt-short
probes.subject: .claude/hooks/_sonnet_classifier.py
probes.note: The off-by-one the loop rewrite invites. Deliberately leaves the constant at 3 so the test's FIRST assertion stays GREEN and this one - the count of calls the transport actually received - reddens alone. Without this probe P3 would witness only that a number is written down, never that it is obeyed.

probes.name: P4-retries-stop-using-the-strict-prompt
probes.subject: .claude/hooks/_sonnet_classifier.py
probes.note: Preserved behaviour, not new: the original single retry used the stricter prompt, and that is why a retry can parse where the first attempt did not. Rewriting the two-branch form into a loop is exactly where this would be dropped silently.

probes.name: P5-http-error-body-discarded-again
probes.subject: .claude/hooks/_sonnet_classifier.py
probes.old: return f"{exc} :: {body[:300]}" if body else str(exc)
probes.note: Restores the shipped behaviour that made 62 logged 500s undiagnosable without an SSH session against MS-S1's server.log. The sibling assertion ('500' in detail) stays GREEN under this mutation - str(exc) still carries the code - so the body claim is witnessed alone, and that green is the positive control proving the reader still runs.
